ἐνδύονται τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν. ἐὰν μέντοι τις παραδοθῇ τῇ κολάσει, οὐδὲν διαφέρει
γυμνοῦ. 2 Kor 5,4 Τὸ ἀκόλουθον θέλει· ἐφ' ὃ ἐπενδύσασθαι θέλομεν τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν,
ἀλλ' οὐκ αὐτὸ τὸ σῶμα ἐκδύσασθαι εἰς φθοράν. διὸ καὶ ἐπήγαγεν· ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ
θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς. 2 Kor 5,5 Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο, δηλονότι εἰς τὸ ἀφθάρτους γενέσθαι.
2 Kor 5,6 Ἀντὶ τοῦ πεπεισμένοι ὅτι ἐπιδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἐν σαρκὶ
ἔτι διάγοντες ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ. 291 2 Kor 5,7 ∆ιὰ πίστεως ἐλπίζομεν εἰς θεόν· οὐ
γὰρ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ὁρατὸν ἡμῖν ἐστιν· τοῦτο δὲ πιστεύομεν ὅτι πρὸς αὐτὸν
ἐκδημήσομεν, ὅτε αὐτὸν ὀψόμεθα καθ' ὅσον ἀνθρώπῳ θεὸν ἰδεῖν δυνατόν.
σωματικῶς γὰρ καὶ Μωϋσῆς εἶδεν, καὶ ἄγγελοι ὁρῶσιν καθὼς αὐτοῖς ὁρᾶν δυνατόν·
θεὸν γὰρ οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε καὶ πᾶν κτίσμα τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπολιμπάνεται
ὄψεως. 2 Kor 5,7–9 Ἐὰν ὧδε ᾖς εὐάρεστος, ἀναντιρρήτως ἐκεῖ εὐαρεστότερος εἶ,
οὐκέτι ἀγωνιζόμενος ἀλλ' ἔχων τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τῆς εὐαρεστήσεως. ἐγχωρεῖ δὲ τὸ διὰ
πίστεως περιπατοῦμεν οὐ διὰ εἴδους καὶ περὶ τῆς οἰκονομίας τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου
εἰρῆσθαι, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς οὐκ ἦν τῶν τεθεαμένων τὸν κύριον ἐν σαρκὶ πρὸ τοῦ πάθους.
2 Kor 5,12 Οἱ ἀρέσκοντες ἀνθρώποις καὶ μὴ δι' αὐτὴν τὴν εὐλάβειαν καυχώμενοι
δηλονότι διὰ πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων καυχῶνται· ἡ γὰρ καρδία ὑπὸ θεοῦ
κατοπτεύεται. 2 Kor 5,13 Ἔκστασιν καλεῖ τὸ καύχημα. καυχώμεθα ἵνα ἐκεῖνος
δοξασθῇ, σιωπῶμεν τὴν καύχησιν– ὅπερ σωφρονεῖν λέγει–ἵνα ὑμᾶς διδάξωμεν μὴ
καυχᾶσθαι. ἔκστασιν δὲ καλεῖ τὸ τὸν ὀφείλοντα φεύγειν τὸ καυχᾶσθαι ἀναγκάζεσθαι
καυχᾶσθαι. Ἔκστασιν λέγει τὸ καύχημα τὸ ἐπὶ τῇ πολιτείᾳ· ἐξεστηκότων γὰρ τὸ
καυχᾶσθαι, σωφρονούντων τὸ μετριάζειν. πολλάκις οὖν ἀναγκαζόμεθα ἐξίστασθαι
καὶ καυχᾶσθαι, ἵνα ὁ θεὸς δι' ἡμῶν δοξασθῇ. σπουδάζομεν δὲ σωφρονεῖν καὶ
μετριάζειν, ἵνα καὶ ὑμᾶς διδάξωμεν μὴ καυχᾶσθαι. ἔκστασιν δὲ λέγει τὸ τὸν
ὀφείλοντα λέγειν τὸ καυχᾶσθαι ἀναγκάζεσθαι εἰς τοῦτο ἔρχεσθαι. 292 2 Kor 5,14–15
Βουλόμενοι σιωπῆσαι ἀναγκαζόμεθα καυχᾶσθαι, συνεχόμενοι ὑπὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ
ἀγάπης, ἵνα ἐκεῖνος δοξάζηται. Οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον· τοὺς πιστοὺς λέγει καὶ διὰ τοῦ
βαπτίσματος καὶ διὰ τῆς ζωῆς νεκρουμένους τῷ κόσμῳ. Καὶ μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν·
καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ εἰ ἐμαυτῷ ἔζων, οὐκ ἐκαυχώμην, ἐπεὶ δὲ Χριστῷ ζῶ, δι' ἐκεῖνον καὶ
σιωπῶ ἂν δέῃ πρὸς τὸ ὑμῶν συμφέρον, δι' ἐκεῖνον καὶ καυχῶμαι, ἵνα ἐκεῖνος
δοξασθῇ. Εἴτε ἐξιστάμεθα, φησίν, εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν ὑμῖν, πάντα διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ
Χριστοῦ πράττομεν. ἐπεὶ οὖν ὁ ὑπὲρ τινῶν ἀποθνήσκων τοὺς ἤδη κατακεκριμένους
θανάτου ἀπαλλάττει, καὶ ὅσον τὸ ἐφ' ἡμῖν ἀποθανόντες ἦμεν, εἰ εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων
ἀπέθανεν. ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον ὅσον τῇ καταδίκῃ. τοὺς πιστοὺς δὲ λέγει οἵτινες
διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἐνεκρώθησαν τῷ κόσμῳ, μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶντες ἀλλὰ τῷ
Χριστῷ· καὶ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν ὑπὲρ πάντων Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ κοινὸν χρέως ἀποδούς,
ἑαυτῷ ὀφειλέτην τὸν κόσμον κατέστησεν. 2 Kor 5,16 Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα
οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα. ἐπειδὴ σαρκὸς ἡ περιτομὴ καὶ τόδε φάγε καὶ τόδε μὴ φάγῃς καὶ
τὸ σάββατον, λέγει ὅτι ἡ μεῖς τῶν πιστῶν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα. ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ
ὑπέκρουε τὸ τὸν κύριον περιτμηθῆναι καὶ τηρῆσαι σάββατον, λέγει τοῦτο εὐκαίρως,
ἵνα τοὺς ἐν νόμῳ ὠφελήσῃ. νῦν δὲ οὐδέπω τοῦτο ... ἔγνωμεν· οὐ γὰρ βούλεται ἡμᾶς
ζῆν κατὰ νόμον. Τοῦτο οὐ μόνον πρὸς τὸ νεκρῶσαι τὰς ἐπιθυμίας εἴρηται, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ
πρὸς τὸ ὑπακούειν ἔτι τῷ νόμῳ· εἰ γὰρ καὶ περιετμήθη Χριστὸς καὶ γέγονεν ὑπὸ τὰς
παρατηρήσεις τοῦ νόμου, ὅ ἐστιν εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν
οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν. ὅτε γὰρ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἦν, ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἐπολιτεύσατο πληρῶν
τὸν νόμον τῷ βίῳ· ἀποθανὼν δὲ καὶ ἀναστὰς ἄφθαρτος κατήργησε τὰ τοῦ νόμου, τῆς
δὲ οὐρανίου πολιτείας ὑπέδειξε τὴν ὁδόν. διὸ καὶ οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι τὰς σωματικὰς
πολιτείας ὡς ἀποθανόντες νεκροῦσιν, 293,ξολ2 τὴν δὲ ἐν οὐρανοῖς καθαρὰν
διαγωγὴν μιμούμενοι συνάπτουσιν ἑαυτοὺς κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν θεῷ. 2 Kor 5,17 Εἴ τις
ἐν Χριστῷ ζῇ καὶ βαπτίζεται, οὗτος καινή ἐστι κτίσις, οὐκέτι κατὰ νόμον ζῶν ἀλλὰ
κατὰ τὴν καινὴν χάριν τοῦ πνεύματος. εἴτε γὰρ εἴποις νόμον εἴτε χάριν, πάντα ἐκ
pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 5:3 note: "All, righteous and unrighteous,] put on the incorruption. If however someone is handed over to the punishment, he differs in nothing from one naked.
[Label 2 Cor 5:4.] He wants the sequence: in that we wish to be clothed over with the incorruption, but not to strip off the body itself into corruption. Therefore he also added: "so that the mortal may be swallowed up by the life."
[Label 2 Cor 5:5.] "Toward this very thing," clearly toward becoming incorruptible.
[Label 2 Cor 5:6.] In place of: being persuaded that, being at home in the body, that is, still passing life in flesh in this world. [Page number 291 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 5:7.] Through faith we hope in God; for his form is not visible to us; but this we believe, that we will go abroad to him, when we will see him, so far as it is possible for a human being to see God. For Moses also saw bodily, and angels see as it is possible for them to see; for no one has ever seen God, and every created thing falls short of the sight of God.
[Label 2 Cor 5:7-9.] If you are well-pleasing here, undeniably you are more well-pleasing there, no longer contending but having the security of the well-pleasing. And it is possible that "we walk through faith, not through sight" was said also about the dispensation of God the Word, since he himself was not among those who had beheld the Lord in flesh before the passion.
[Label 2 Cor 5:12.] Those pleasing people and boasting not on account of reverence itself clearly boast on account of the face of people; for the heart is watched over by God.
[Label 2 Cor 5:13.] He calls the boast "being beside oneself." We boast so that that one may be glorified; we keep the boasting silent (which he calls being of sound mind) so that we may teach you not to boast. And he calls "being beside oneself" the one who ought to flee boasting being compelled to boast.
[Second form of the same note, not marked. New material:] He calls "being beside oneself" the boast about the way of life; for boasting is of those beside themselves, being moderate is of those of sound mind. [Repeats: often then we are compelled to be beside ourselves and to boast, so that God may be glorified through us; but we are eager to be of sound mind and moderate, so that we may teach you also not to boast; and he calls "being beside oneself" the one who ought to "speak" (λέγειν, where the first form has "flee") the boasting being compelled to come to this.] [Page number 292 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 5:14-15.] Wishing to keep silent, we are compelled to boast, being held together by the love of Christ, so that that one may be glorified. "All died": he means the faithful, being made dead to the world both through baptism and through their life. "And no longer live for themselves": for I too, if I lived for myself, would not boast; but since I live for Christ, on account of him I both keep silent, if need be, toward your advantage, and on account of him I boast, so that that one may be glorified. "Whether we are beside ourselves," he says, "or are of sound mind for you," we do all things on account of the love of Christ. Since then the one dying on behalf of some frees those already condemned from death, and as far as it lay with us we were dead, if one died for all, then all died, so far as the sentence. And he means the faithful, who through baptism were made dead to the world, no longer living for themselves but for Christ; for Christ, having died on behalf of all and having paid the common debt, made the world a debtor to himself.
[Label 2 Cor 5:16.] "So that we from now know no one according to flesh." Since circumcision is of the flesh, and "eat this" and "do not eat this," and the sabbath, he says that we of the faithful know no one according to flesh. But since the Lord's being circumcised and keeping sabbath was an obstacle, he says this opportunely, so as to benefit those in the law. "But now not yet this [gap in the Greek] we knew"; for he does not want us to live according to law. This was said not only toward putting to death the desires, but toward no longer obeying the law either; for even if Christ was circumcised and came under the observances of the law, which is "even if we have known Christ according to flesh, yet now we no longer know." For when he was among people, as a man he lived as a citizen, fulfilling the law by his life; but having died and risen incorruptible, he abolished the things of the law, and showed the way of the heavenly citizenship. Therefore those being baptized also, as having died, put to death the bodily ways of life, [column mark 293 col. 2 dropped] and imitating the pure life in the heavens join themselves to God according to the heart.
[Label 2 Cor 5:17.] If anyone lives in Christ and is baptized, this one is a new creation, no longer living according to law but according to the new grace of the Spirit. For whether you should say law or grace, all things from ... [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … put on incorruption. But if anyone is handed over to punishment, he is no better off than a naked man.

On 2 Corinthians 5:4: He means the thought to run on like this: we want to be clothed over with incorruption, not to strip off the body itself into corruption. That is why he added, “so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.”
On 2 Corinthians 5:5: “For this very thing”: that is, for becoming incorruptible.
On 2 Corinthians 5:6: It stands for “being persuaded that while we are at home in the body,” that is, while we still live in the flesh in this world.

On 2 Corinthians 5:7: By faith we hope in God, for his form is not visible to us. But we believe that we will leave home and go to him, and then we will see him as far as a human being can see God. Moses, too, saw in a bodily way, and angels see as far as they are able to see; for no one has ever seen God (John 1:18), and every creature falls short of seeing God.

On 2 Corinthians 5:7–9: If you are pleasing here, beyond question you are more pleasing there, no longer struggling but secure in pleasing. It is also possible that “we walk by faith, not by sight” was said about the dispensation of God the Word, since Paul himself was not among those who had seen the Lord in the flesh before the passion.
On 2 Corinthians 5:12: Those who please people, and do not boast for the sake of reverence itself, plainly boast for show before people; for God watches the heart.

On 2 Corinthians 5:13: He calls boasting “being beside ourselves.” We boast so that he may be glorified; we say nothing of our boasting, and this he calls being of sound mind, so that we may teach you not to boast. He calls it “being beside oneself” when one who ought to shun boasting is forced to boast.
The second catena form adds: He means boasting about one's way of life. Boasting belongs to people who are beside themselves; moderation belongs to people of sound mind.

On 2 Corinthians 5:14–15: We would rather keep silent, but we are forced to boast, held fast by the love of Christ, so that he may be glorified. “All died”: he means the faithful, who are made dead to the world through baptism and through their way of life. “And no longer live for themselves”: for if I lived for myself, I would not boast either; but since I live for Christ, I keep silent for his sake when your good requires it, and for his sake I also boast, so that he may be glorified. “Whether we are beside ourselves,” he says, “or of sound mind for you,” we do everything because of the love of Christ. Now one who dies for others frees from death those already condemned, and as far as it lay with us, we were dead. If one died for all, then all died, as far as the sentence goes. He means the faithful, who through baptism were made dead to the world and no longer live for themselves but for Christ. For Christ, by dying for all and paying the common debt, made the world his debtor.

On 2 Corinthians 5:16: “So that from now on we know no one according to the flesh.” Circumcision belongs to the flesh, and so do “eat this” and “do not eat that,” and the sabbath; so he says that we who believe know no one according to the flesh. But since it could be objected that the Lord was circumcised and kept the sabbath, he says this at the right moment, to help those who are under the law. “But now we have not yet […] known this”: for he does not want us to live by the law. This was said not only to put our desires to death but also so that we no longer obey the law. For even if Christ was circumcised and came under the observances of the law, that is, “even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no longer.” When he was among men, he lived as a man and fulfilled the law in his life; but when he died and rose incorruptible, he abolished what belongs to the law and showed the way of the heavenly life. That is why the baptized, as people who have died, put to death the bodily ways of living, and by imitating the pure life of heaven they join themselves to God in their hearts.

On 2 Corinthians 5:17: If anyone lives in Christ and is baptized, he is a new creation, living no longer by the law but by the new grace of the Spirit. For whether you say law or grace, all things are from …
notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss, printed the 5:13 note twice, and put '(2 Cor 5:5)' after the 5:4 words 'so that the mortal might be swallowed up by life'. Doublet collapsed: 5:13 (first form kept; the second form's new sentences printed under 'The second catena form adds:'; it reads λέγειν where the first reads φεύγειν). The two 5:16 notes and the repeated 'faithful made dead through baptism' phrase in 5:14-15 belong to different notes and are kept. The Greek gap in the 5:16 lemma is kept as […]. Labels one per note (5:4 to 5:17); page and column marks dropped; section opens and ends mid-sentence with '…'.

lemmas.gloss: raise an objection, stand in the way

choices.why: “so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life” is 5:4; the old English printed (2 Cor 5:5) after it. The edition labels 5:4 and 5:5 separately.

choices.english: first form kept; the new sentences (boasting about one's way of life; boasting belongs to the beside-themselves, moderation to the sober) printed under 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Brief doublet rule. The second form's last sentence has λέγειν where the first has φεύγειν; recorded, not printed twice.
'He means the faithful, made dead to the world through baptism' occurs twice, but the second time inside a different argument (the one dying for all); the two are different notes, so both stay.
The second ('This was said not only ...') argues differently and is not a second form of the first.

choices.english: “But now we have not yet […] known this”
choices.why: The Greek marks a gap; οὐδέπω is kept as printed ('not yet'), nothing supplied.

choices.english: so that he may be glorified
choices.why: ἐκεῖνος (Christ, by the next note's 'love of Christ') kept as a pronoun; no name supplied.
rejected: so that Christ may be glorified
